templates.title: Crush (Native Anthropic)
templates.instructions: Place at ~/.config/crush/crush.json. Pick this variant for Claude models — Crush's `type: "anthropic"` provider preserves thinking blocks and prompt-cache hints that the OpenAI-compatible path drops. `supports_attachments` and `can_reason` reflect the route's resolved capabilities. `models.large` is the gateway's default model and `models.small`, which Crush uses for its lighter work, the gateway's fast model (each the default model until an admin fills that slot on the route). Usage metrics and the provider-list refresh from Charm are off (`options.disable_metrics`, `options.disable_provider_auto_update`); an admin who wants them back can edit this template.

templates.title: Crush (OpenAI-compatible)
templates.instructions: Place at ~/.config/crush/crush.json (global) or .crush.json in a project. Works with every model the gateway serves. Crush's `type: "openai"` provider does not pass through reasoning blocks or prompt-cache control. Each model declares `supports_attachments` (vision) and `can_reason` explicitly — Crush uses these to gate image input and chain-of-thought UI. If the underlying route doesn't advertise vision capability the flag renders `false` and Crush hides the attach-image affordance. `models.large` is the gateway's default model and `models.small`, which Crush uses for its lighter work, the gateway's fast model (each the default model until an admin fills that slot on the route). Usage metrics and the provider-list refresh from Charm are off (`options.disable_metrics`, `options.disable_provider_auto_update`); an admin who wants them back can edit this template.

templates.title: Crush · MCP only (static key)
templates.instructions: Merge into ~/.config/crush/crush.json alongside any existing providers block. No LLM key is minted in this flow. Usage metrics and the provider-list refresh from Charm are off (`options.disable_metrics`, `options.disable_provider_auto_update`); an admin who wants them back can edit this template.
